title: Version-Aware Normalization of Findings Against MITRE ATT&CK v19
subtitle: Typed Data Models and Revocation-Resolving Technique Lookup for Security Tooling

cards.label: source remap entries, including 22 release revocations
new-technique entries in repository migration table

contribution: A typed ATT&CK v19 data layer that normalizes findings across version churn by resolving revoked/renamed technique IDs through a maintained remap table over SHA-256-verified STIX data, with indexed lookup for downstream security tooling.
methods: Download/validate ATT&CK STIX data with SHA-256 verification.
Parse techniques/tactics/platform metadata into typed structures.
Resolve deprecated/revoked IDs through the v19 remap table.
Build in-memory indexes for ID, tactic, platform, and keyword lookup.
Regression-test migration and data-loader behavior across supported Python versions.
evidence: Cited Python 3.12 CI: 165 passed; 63.83% statement coverage, same test job.
Current source inventory: 22 release-revocation entries, 29 total remaps and 46 V19_NEW_TECHNIQUES entries. The earlier 48 figure was not the implemented table count.
The alleged release-wide total of 48 was not independently verified from official STIX/release evidence; this poster reports the repository table only.
Loader/index code performs pinned STIX validation and lookup; local full STIX-dependent execution remains blocked by missing data.
limitations: ATT&CK mapping/normalization does not prove an attack occurred.
O(1) dictionary/index lookup describes the in-memory data structure, not end-to-end system latency.
Future ATT&CK releases require new migration/remap evidence.
reproduction: Install the documented development dependencies; run python -m pytest tests/ -q. Use the cited job configuration when reproducing coverage.
Benchmark data, adapters and environment requirements are separate; consult poster/13_reproducibility.md and the claim ledger.
